name: Beau Han Bridge
bio: Beau Han Bridge is a filmmaker, actor and theatre artist and founder of Midtwenties Productions. His documentary She Sings for the World (2023) screened at the Beijing International Short Film Festival, Vancouver Asian Film Festival and San Diego Asian Film Festival. He stars as Zane in CBC/Shaftesbury's Macy Murdoch.

credits.title: Moving Matter: Horizons
credits.overview: An experimental dance film exploring subterranean worlds through the materiality of tarp. Bodies and fabric intertwine in a choreographic dialogue, transforming ideas of shelter, landscape, and the shifting spaces beneath our feet.

credits.title: Investigations of a Breakup
credits.overview: Sophia struggles with overthinking her life as a poor, nihilistic drifter. Exiled to a life of solitude, she has the chance to change it all upon meeting Liza one night...  Did she let her in or was she destined to burn it all? The aftermath of their breakup is explored through three different angles.

credits.title: The SAS
credits.overview: On February 20th, 2016, a college student's friend goes missing. Through phone recordings, we recall the event that led up to his disappearance.

credits.title: Moving Matter: Soil
credits.overview: An experimental dance film exploring soil as a living, shifting material, revealing its choreographic intelligence through movement, costume, sound, and film.

credits.title: Macy Murdoch: Back to the Past
credits.overview: Macy and friends find the mysteriously re-built time machine and travel to the past only to find a dead Macy in the morgue! Using forensic clues, Macy must stop her own death from happening.

credits.title: Macy Murdoch: A Murder Rewritten
credits.overview: When a mysterious rival uses a time machine to frame famous Edwardian-era Detective William Murdoch of a murder he didn’t commit, Macy Murdoch and her friends travel back to 1910 to determine the real perpetrator of the crime.

credits.title: Moving Matter: Wool
credits.overview: An experimental dance film exploring wool as a material of transformation, memory, and connection.

credits.title: Daughters & Sons
credits.overview: A daughter struggles to speak with her father about her grandmother, revealing the quiet distances — and shared inheritances — that shape three generations of family.

credits.title: Habitus Fragments
credits.overview: As a city dweller goes about her morning routine, transience, fluidity of economic change, gentrification, decay, and dislocated tensions that encompass the Victory Square today are dreamt upon seeing a stranger outside in the courtyard.

credits.title: A Greater Chance
credits.overview: Upon learning of his father's terminal illness diagnosis, a young, autistic, hearing-impaired artist travels back to Taiwan with a filmmaker to make a film in his honour.

credits.title: A Bunch of Times
credits.overview: Discomfort abounds when a middle-aged stepfather attempts to connect with his teenage stepson the only way he knows how: with sexually-charged humour.

credits.title: Persephone Mara
credits.overview: A surreal romance about two adolescents named Persephone and Mara, who decide to escape from the world around them by locking themselves away in an old projector room at the Cinematheque.

credits.title: Moving Matter: Linoleum
credits.overview: An experimental dance film tracing the transformation of discarded 1950s kitchen flooring into costumes and shelters, unsettling ideals of domestic stability and revealing the anxieties lurking beneath a seemingly orderly world.

credits.title: She Sings for the World
credits.overview: A Chinese Canadian son sets out to make a film on his mother, who was once known as the first ever Chinese Opera Singer to have performed Pingju Opera in English in late 1980's China.

credits.title: Love Evolving
credits.overview: An anxious woman navigates the bustle of modern day Cairo to find her missing lover, a young adult strives for an authentic connection in a future society numbed by alcohol, and two Cold War-era lovers face the consequences of finding romance across political borders. A vibrant collection of short films - by turns grit

credits.title: Ice, Skating
credits.overview: A young boy comes to terms with grief, but the ice cracks beneath, as surfaces of the past reform once again.

credits.title: Recollections
credits.overview: A mother remembers her brother as her son comes to terms with his partner.

credits.title: Beneath a Rougher Sea
credits.overview: Two radical youths embark on a journey to a house on a mountain.

credits.title: The Threshing Floor
credits.overview: Set to a score by Mauricio Pauly (The Threshing Floor), multiple microphones, choreographic sequences, scores, and projected images, we are enveloped into a multimodal experience of two bodies in space.

credits.title: Lone Scholar in the Autumn Woods
credits.overview: Second year film assignment inspired by the 1948 painting “Lone Scholar in the Autumn Woods” by Zhang Da Qian.

credits.title: Hot Seat
credits.overview: A short documentary that explores the art of being "put on the spot". Six different people are brought together and take turns asking each other personal questions that they wouldn't ask otherwise.

credits.title: Above the Hospital: The Workshop
credits.overview: An experimental workshopping of Act One in Beau Han Bridge's play "Above The Hospital" by local Vancouver actors.

credits.title: Moving Out
credits.overview: A Mother helps her daughter move out into a new apartment.

credits.title: The Divine Tragedy of Digital Youth
credits.overview: Two modern youngsters try to seek closure on their failed relationship in a crowded club filled with digital zombie youths.

credits.title: The Human Voice
credits.overview: A film adaptation of the one-woman play by Jean Cocteau starring Shelby Satterthwaite as a woman who deals with the emotional turmoils of talking to her lover one last time over the phone.

credits.title: Two Lonely Kids
credits.overview: Two lonely kids named Jemma and Todd spend a day recording a song together.

credits.title: The Red Coat
credits.overview: A short film adaptation of the play of the same name by John Patrick Shanley (From the one-act collection “Welcome To The Moon”)

credits.title: Reminder
credits.overview: Nic wakes up to a reminder. Kay reads the reminder.

credits.title: Margot's Period
credits.overview: At a house party, Margot’s seemingly ordinary night takes a disturbing turn as she experiences the horrors of getting her first period in public.

credits.title: Homecoming
credits.overview: A film that depicts the very first day of a Chinese foreign-exchange student living abroad.

credits.title: Ocean
credits.overview: five millennials mirror one another in this experimental docudrama shot around the oceanic edges of Vancouver, BC, Canada.

credits.title: Death Note
credits.overview: Light Turner finds a supernatural notebook and uses it to mete out death, attracting the attention of a detective, a demon and a girl in his class.

credits.title: Siblings
credits.overview: Two siblings get together for an evening after not seeing each other for 2 years. Interesting conversations ensue.

credits.title: The Songwriter
credits.overview: Elizabeth Rose has a secret passion for writing songs in her apartment, but her insecurities lead her to never telling anyone who they are about. One day, that person arrives.

credits.title: Reading Una
credits.overview: Two lonely kids get together for a study session. As time flies and moments of connection ensue, does it signify something more?

credits.title: Love Is All
credits.overview: Anna wastes her day in her apartment as she waits to see her boyfriend later. A short mumblecore drama about clinging to connection.

credits.title: Making a Bed Shirtless
credits.overview: One-Shot Film of an original one act about three roommates who spend a Sunday afternoon together talking about various things. Interesting moments ensue.
